top.headline: Lean groups say the Claude-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof checks out
top.why: The claim from Friday is no longer a lone author's word: a formal proof checker has accepted it. Human mathematicians still have to understand it, and the Clay prize rules are a long way off.
points: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge posted a four-page note on 20 Nov saying Claude helped him prove the Riemann hypothesis over about six weeks, with the full proof written in Lean.
On 21 Nov the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative said they have 'full confidence' it is correct, after reproducing the proof export and checking the statement matches Mathlib's definition.

Mathematicians split on the write-up: James Maynard (Oxford) expects it to hold; Andrew Granville called the note garbled (Nature). A rival human-written preprint by Alessandro Maria Masullo appeared the same day.
Clay Institute rules need publication and a two-year wait, so the $1m prize is not settled; Anthropic had not commented, per the reports.
top.next: Alpöge's promised human-readable write-up (no date given); Anthropic shares reopen Mon 23 Nov, 6:30 AM PT.

stories.headline: Instagram quietly adds Shein, Lowe's and Halara to native affiliate links
stories.why: Affiliate tagging on Instagram is now more than Amazon, with commission rates well above Amazon's for some brands. DTC brands can be tagged by creators if they run an affiliate programme and keep a Meta catalogue.
points: Amazon's integration launched 16 Nov; Business Insider reported on 18 Nov that Shein, Lowe's and Halara were added without announcement.
Rates seen by Business Insider: Amazon 1-4%, Shein 2%, Halara 10%, Lowe's 8-25%. Brands and networks set them; Instagram says it takes no cut.
Lowe's and Halara run through Impact.com, up to 30 products per reel. With a Meta catalogue the link becomes a native product tag; without one it shows as a sticker.
US creators only for Amazon and Impact.com; 18+ with a public professional account, and a 1,000+ follower minimum for some programmes.
stories.next: No date set; watch for further brands or a Meta announcement.

stories.headline: 15,000-year-old Natufian clay figurines found to carry children's fingerprints
stories.why: Pushes the clay-figurine tradition in Southwest Asia back by up to 3,000 years and shows adults and children making symbolic objects before farming. It is evidence for early ritual and storytelling in the Levant, though the meaning of the figures is interpretation.
points: Hebrew University study of 154 Natufian clay figurines from Eynan-Mallaha, Hayonim Terrace and el-Wad Terrace; 15 are recognisable, 139 are cylindrical fragments
Microscopic fingerprints show both adults and children, some probably under 10, helped shape and decorate them
Of the 15 identifiable pieces, 11 are birds; others are a gazelle, a mammal and two human forms; red engobe colouring dated to 15,000 years ago is the earliest known
Researchers suggest a role in belief, seasonal knowledge and storytelling; that reading is interpretation, not established fact
stories.next: No dated catalyst; watch for the peer-reviewed publication details and follow-up comment from the IAA.

stories.headline: Chinese pastor Gao Quanfu left in custody after trial ends without verdict
stories.why: A live global-Christianity persecution case showing the growing use of fraud charges rather than ideological ones against church leaders in China.
points: Gao Quanfu, 70, pastor of Light of Zion church in Xi'an for over 40 years, faces fraud charges at Beilin District People's Court; up to 13 years if convicted
Detained May 2025; his wife Pang Yu was arrested in September 2025
Christian Solidarity Worldwide says lawyers were pressured, some dropped the case, and the pre-trial lasted under half a day; it has health concerns for Pang Yu
No verdict or details of their location have been released; the account relies on CSW, an advocacy group
stories.next: A verdict is awaited; no date given.

stories.headline: Childhood head-scan radiation linked to small rise in brain tumour risk, JAMA cohort of 3.7m
stories.why: A large dose-response finding that supports asking whether a child's scan is needed and whether ultrasound or MRI could do instead. The absolute risk is small and it is no reason to refuse a necessary scan.
points: JAMA, 19 Nov: radiation equal to one head CT linked to 1.8-fold higher brain tumour risk, about 8 extra tumours per 10,000 children by age 21
Over 3.7 million children born 1996-2016 across six US and Ontario health systems, followed 12.3 years on average; 1,536 brain tumours, 82.5% aggressive
Authors estimate about 10% of childhood brain tumours in the cohort are attributable to imaging radiation; a head CT averaged about 66 mGy to the brain
Does not change current guidance; a JAMA editorial says cumulative dose should not become an automatic threshold
stories.next: No dated catalyst; watch for guideline or radiology-society response.
stories.study: Observational cohort, n>3.7 million children, US and Ontario; key limitation: confounding by indication (children scanned may already have symptoms linked to tumours), association not causation

stories.headline: GTA VI crashes on PS5 with error CE-108255-1; neither Sony nor Rockstar has responded
stories.why: The biggest launch ever is hitting a hardware or software fault on some PS5 consoles, with players bounced between Sony and Rockstar support. It matters for anyone on a launch-era PS5 and for how Rockstar patches.
points: Reports since launch on 19 Nov: crashes at start-up, in the opening cutscene and early missions, mostly base PS5 and Slim, some PS5 Pro
Sony's guidance is only 'try updating your game'; Rockstar's troubleshooting page (updated 18 Nov) just links to Sony and Microsoft

Based on player reports collected by Notebookcheck, not a confirmed fault
